working_title: Keeping local history alive in different ways

exercise.instructions: You are going to read four profiles of people involved in preserving local history. For questions 43–52, choose from the profiles A–D. The profiles may be chosen more than once.
exercise.matching_intro: Read the following profiles of people involved in preserving local history. Answer the questions by matching each statement to one of the profiles A–D.

A.label: A
A.text: I started volunteering to record oral histories after a chat with an elderly neighbour opened my eyes to how many personal stories are never documented. My goal is to capture these experiences before they vanish. However, it can be challenging when interviewees drift from dates and facts to personal memories, which are sometimes difficult to verify. I’ve learned to ask open-ended questions and cross-check basic facts where possible. While I value these ordinary memories more than famous events, I’ve become more cautious about separating memory from fact.

B.label: B
B.text: I joined the team restoring our old community cinema when I saw it closed and neglected. I wanted to protect a place that holds shared memories for so many locals. The work is slower and less glamorous than I imagined, but I enjoy the practical teamwork involved. We clean and repair what we can, though some modern changes are necessary for it to function again. I’ve come to accept these compromises if it means the building can be used once more.

C.label: C
C.text: My journey began when I discovered boxes of old family and street photographs. I wanted to make these scattered images searchable and accessible, so I created a digital archive. The biggest challenge is that many photos lack dates or names, and online descriptions can easily become guesses. I invite residents to help identify people and places, ensuring uncertain information is clearly marked. It’s most satisfying when small clues come together to identify an image.

D.label: D
D.text: Organising local walking tours started when friends kept asking about the unusual buildings in our neighbourhood. My aim is to help residents notice the history around them. The difficulty lies in keeping tours engaging without turning uncertain stories into facts. I build routes around visible details and adjust the pace according to the group. While I believe curiosity is important, trust matters more, so I leave out stories that cannot be supported.

questions.prompt: Which person started their project because they were inspired by a neighbour's stories?
questions.evidence: A chat with an elderly neighbour opened my eyes to how many personal stories are never documented.
questions.rationale: Profile A mentions being inspired by a neighbour's stories, which prompted them to start recording oral histories.

questions.prompt: Who finds satisfaction in connecting small clues to identify something?
questions.evidence: It’s most satisfying when small clues come together to identify an image.
questions.rationale: Profile C describes the satisfaction of using small clues to identify images in their digital archive.

questions.prompt: Which person had to accept that some modern changes were necessary for their project?
questions.evidence: Some modern changes are necessary for it to function again.
questions.rationale: Profile B discusses the necessity of modern changes to restore the community cinema.

questions.prompt: Who believes that curiosity is important but trust is more important?
questions.evidence: While I believe curiosity is important, trust matters more.
questions.rationale: Profile D emphasises the importance of trust over curiosity in organising walking tours.

questions.prompt: Which person enjoys the teamwork aspect of their project?
questions.evidence: I enjoy the practical teamwork involved.
questions.rationale: Profile B mentions enjoying the teamwork involved in restoring the cinema.

questions.prompt: Who faces challenges with interviewees straying from facts to personal memories?
questions.evidence: Interviewees drift from dates and facts to personal memories.
questions.rationale: Profile A describes the challenge of interviewees straying from factual information to personal memories.

questions.prompt: Who invites local residents to help with their project?
questions.evidence: I invite residents to help identify people and places.
questions.rationale: Profile C involves local residents in identifying people and places in the photo archive.

questions.prompt: Which person had friends asking them about local history, prompting their involvement?
questions.evidence: Friends kept asking about the unusual buildings in our neighbourhood.
questions.rationale: Profile D began organising walking tours because friends asked about local history.

questions.prompt: Who has learned to ask open-ended questions in their work?
questions.evidence: I’ve learned to ask open-ended questions.
questions.rationale: Profile A mentions learning to ask open-ended questions during interviews.

questions.prompt: Which person had to label uncertain information clearly to avoid guesses?
questions.evidence: Ensuring uncertain information is clearly marked.
questions.rationale: Profile C talks about clearly marking uncertain information in the digital photo archive.
